## Follow-up Comments
Assert that default findings keep the object's labels and annotations.
`1-36`: **📐 Maintainability & Code Quality** | **🔵 Trivial** | **⚡ Quick win** **Assert that default findings keep the object's labels and annotations.** `test_default_finding_keeps_the_subject_of_the_changed_object` checks the subject name and namespace, but not `subject.labels` or `subject.annotations`. The fixture has nonempty values for both. A regression that drops either field from `K8sBaseChangeEvent.get_subject()` would still pass this test. The linked issue requires both fields to be preserved.
Suggested fix ```diff assert finding.subject.namespace == obj.metadata.namespace assert finding.attribute_map["namespace"] == obj.metadata.namespace + assert finding.subject.labels == obj.metadata.labels + assert finding.subject.annotations == obj.metadata.annotations ```

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Preserve the fallback for concrete change events.** `PodChangeEvent(operation=K8sOperationType.DELETE).create_default_finding()` raises `AttributeError` when `obj` is absent. Its generated `get_subject()` override dereferences `self.obj` before the new fallback can run. Other concrete change events have the same override. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robusta-dev/robusta/dbe490a2b93755f3d4e610041015ad1147a3ecf2/src/robusta/integrations/kubernetes/autogenerated/events.py)) Make the generated overrides use the guarded base implementation, or guard this call. Add a no-object test for a concrete change event.
